ops.title: yasyf box synckit root cause (corrected): dev synckitd shadow + TWO distinct peer failures (manifest name vs protocol revision)
ops.body:
Supersedes the earlier "FINAL" note — the "neither peer has rpc-serve" claim was wrong (Cobra hides subcommands from --help; only direct invocation settles existence).

**Fact base**: `which -a synckitd` on the yasyf box resolves `~/.local/share/mise/installs/go/1.26.5/bin/synckitd` FIRST — a `go install` dev build (Jul 24 22:17, swarm's last night, `9999.…-dev`) shadowing brew 0.35.2. The dev daemon demands the v1 state envelope (Jul 3 state.json predates it) and the revisioned sync-RPC protocol.

**The two peer failures are DIFFERENT despite identical-looking log lines**:
- **reposync 0.27.3**: already adopted the revisioned protocol — exposes `rpc-serve-v1`, no longer answers `rpc-serve`. Its MANIFEST still says `rpc-serve` → child dies with `unknown command`. Fix = manifest, not binary: `reposync install` regenerates the manifest from the binary's own command set.
- **cc-pool 0.61.7**: `cc-pool sync rpc-serve` EXISTS (hidden subcommand, exit 0, "Bridge sync RPC frames … used by synckitd") — its manifest is correct and the child STARTS. Its `handshake failed: read acknowledge: EOF` is a wire-protocol mismatch: pre-revision cc-pool vs the dev synckitd expecting the revisioned service. Fix = a cc-pool RELEASE that speaks the revisioned protocol (manifest rewrite would not help).

**Refined yasyf-box repair order**: (1) remove the shadowing dev synckitd so brew resolves; (2) brew upgrade synckit/cc-pool/reposync to the baseline-pinned releases from A5; (3) regenerate manifests via each binary's own registration path (`reposync install`, `cc-pool sync enable`) instead of hand-editing JSON; (4) `synckitd host add` to migrate state to the v1 envelope (preserve peer yasyf@yasyf-home); (5) restart serve/reconcile/cookiesync and watch failure counts go to zero.

**A4/A5 checklist addition**: before cutting the A5 releases, VERIFY synckit-main ↔ cc-pool-main ↔ reposync-main agree on the sync-RPC protocol revision — the swarm died mid-migration of this contract (reposync moved, cc-pool didn't, synckit only in a dev build). Releases cut from mains that disagree would reproduce this exact failure at the new baseline.
